subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Ferrari's Origin Story
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Ferrari's Origin Story.

hook.text: Enzo Ferrari didn't start a car company to sell cars. He sold cars to fund his racing team.

buildup.text: Ferrari raced for Alfa Romeo in the 1930s. When they dropped him, he started building his own cars.

discovery.text: His first road car, the 125 S in 1947, used a V12 engine. It won its second ever race.

twist.text: Enzo famously insulted a customer named Ferruccio Lamborghini—who then built his own supercar company.

climax.text: That rivalry pushed both brands to make faster, more beautiful cars for decades.

punchline.text: One insult created Ferrari's greatest competitor.

quiz.question: Why did Lamborghini start a car company?
options: To beat Ford at Le Mans

details.summary: Enzo Ferrari founded his legendary car company in 1947 after being fired from Alfa Romeo's racing team, channeling his obsession with speed into building the world's most iconic sports cars.
details.whyItMatters: Ferrari set the standard for automotive passion and exclusivity. The brand proved that racing heritage and limited production could create value far beyond transportation.
takeaways: Enzo Ferrari raced for Alfa Romeo before starting his own firm
The first Ferrari road car was the 1947 125 S
Racing success became Ferrari's primary marketing strategy

faq.question: Why is the Ferrari logo a prancing horse?
faq.answer: The Cavallino Rampante was originally the emblem of a World War I Italian fighter ace. His family offered it to Enzo Ferrari as a good luck charm for his racing cars, and it became the brand's icon.

faq.question: Why do Ferraris hold their value so well?
faq.answer: Ferrari deliberately limits production to maintain scarcity. Combined with racing prestige, craftsmanship, and a passionate collector community, used Ferraris often appreciate rather than depreciate.
